text:
alex: Quick heads-up — I ran a small audit and found ~12 ownerless service keys across our AWS org and a handful of KMS grants that are effectively admin. Thinking we should schedule a focused access review + entitlement cleanup this week. Thoughts?

maria: thanks for flagging. can you paste the exact query or script you used so we can reproduce?

alex: sure. I used our inventory script that checks tags + last-used + attached principals. Short example: 
```
python tools/iam_audit/ownerless_keys.py --accounts 111122223333,222233334444 --min-unused-days 90 --output csv
```
It flags keys with no `tag:owner` and last_used > 120d. found ~12 across prod and staging.

kevin: good catch. do we have enforced tag rules at creation time? possible that infra svc accounts slip through.

sara: we have a tag policy but it's advisory, not enforced. for private deployments customers sometimes create service accts without tags. my suggestion: 1) inventory+classify 2) notify owners 3) temp-disable stale keys 90d+ 4) delete after confirmation.

alex: proposed plan:
1) Run full inventory + classify (ownerless vs stale vs active) and produce CSV
2) Auto-create Jira ticket per flagged key and DM owner via infra-bot (48h response window)
3) Canary: disable keys older than 90d on Friday morning, monitor 24h, then delete after 72h if no regression
4) RBAC follow-up: identify any principals with broad KMS permissions and propose least-priv changes (diffs)
5) Attach audit logs (CloudTrail) for last 365d for each principal to the ticket for triage

maria: sounds reasonable. how do we want to notify app owners? slack DM + email + jira?

kevin: infra-bot can create the Jira issues and DM them. infra-bot: can you create issues when fed a CSV?

infra-bot: yes. use `infra-bot create_issue --project SEC --file ownerless_keys.csv --template ownerless-key` will create one issue per row and DM the owner if found.

sara: note on KMS grants: some service roles have `kms:Decrypt` + `kms:GenerateDataKey*` scoped to `arn:aws:kms:*:*:key/*` — we should tighten to specific key ARNs and add caller-account conditions where feasible. also watch for grants created with `RetiringPrincipal` or cross-account principals.

alex: example IAM policy change I want to propose for affected services:
```
- Effect: Allow
  Action: kms:*
  Resource: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/*
+ Effect: Allow
  Action: ["kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey"]
  Resource: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/abcd-1234
```
This reduces blast radius instead of allowing `kms:*` on all keys.

kevin: one of the flagged keys is referenced by a CI job that pulls private images. we need to coordinate with CI owners before disabling. rotation-in-place might be best there.

sara: agree. for CI/infra keys we do: rotate -> update pipeline -> validate -> disable old key. for unknown/ownerless keys we do disable -> 24h monitor -> delete.

alex: timeline: inventory + jira creation today, disable sweep Friday 09:00 PT, delete sweep following Tuesday (gives time for remediation). ok?

maria: :+1: can you also draft an email template and the DM copy?

alex: drafting now, sample email: 
```
Subject: Action required — Service access key flagged as ownerless (acct-111122223333)
Hi — we've detected a service access key in account acct-111122223333 that lacks an owner tag and hasn't been used in 140 days. We'll disable the key on 2026-05-14 09:00 PT unless you claim or open a ticket. Reply to this message or add owner in the Jira ticket: SEC-XXXX.
If this key is used by CI or a production pipeline, please respond immediately and follow the runbook here: https://wiki.redwood/ops/keys-runbook
```

sec-bot: created SEC-4923 for acct-111122223333 ownerless-key. Link: https://rwd.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-4923 :eyes:

kevin: please include the runbook link in the Jira template and a rollback checklist.

sara: also add a KMS grant audit snippet to the runbook. example CLI: 
```
aws kms list-grants --key-id alias/our-key --query 'Grants[?starts_with(GranteePrincipal, `arn:aws:iam::`) == `true`]'
```
and for policy scanning: `policy-scan --fixable --output json | jq '.[] | select(.severity=="HIGH")'`

alex: I'll attach the inventory CSV and the proposed policy diffs to SEC-4923 in the next 20m and post the notification drafts here for review. tagging @security-oncall for visibility.

security-oncall: noted, will put extra eyeballs on alerts during the disable window and standby for rollback if we see increased error rates.

maria: thanks team. concise plan — let's run the inventory now and iterate.
